title: AP Non-Tax Revenue – Sources, Trends and Post-Bifurcation Limits
bullets: **Non-tax revenue** = a State's own receipts that are **not taxes**: **interest receipts**, **dividends and profits** of State enterprises, **fees, fines and user charges**, and receipts of departmental services (**mines, forests, irrigation, power**).
**State's own revenue = own tax revenue + own non-tax revenue**; the **share in central taxes** and **grants-in-aid** are **central transfers**, not own non-tax revenue.
Common decoys: **State GST, VAT on petrol, State excise, stamps and registration, taxes on vehicles** are all **tax** revenue, not non-tax revenue.
**AP own non-tax revenue:** **₹5,972 crore (2024-25 actuals)** → ₹19,119 crore (2025-26 BE) → **₹14,324 crore (2025-26 RE**, about 25% below BE) → **₹11,474 crore (2026-27 BE)**.
**AP Budget 2026-27 own revenue** = own tax **₹1,25,846 crore** + own non-tax **₹11,474 crore** = **₹1,37,320 crore**.
**Total revenue receipts 2026-27 BE: ₹2,34,140 crore** – own tax about 54%, **share in central taxes ₹64,362 crore**, **grants-in-aid ₹32,458 crore**; own non-tax revenue only **about 5%**.
**Largest non-tax head = mines and minerals**: **₹5,320 crore (2025-26 RE)** and **₹5,196 crore (2026-27 BE)** – about **45%** of AP's non-tax revenue.

Mining receipts: **royalty** on major minerals and **seigniorage fee** on **minor minerals** (stone, gravel, sand) collected by the **Department of Mines and Geology**; **APMDC** (AP Mineral Development Corporation) is the State mining PSU that runs the **Mangampet barytes** mines (Rayalaseema).

**Supreme Court, 25 July 2024 – Mineral Area Development Authority v. SAIL** (nine judges, **8:1**): **royalty is not a tax**; **States can tax mineral rights and mineral-bearing land** (overruling India Cement, 1989) – widens the State's mineral revenue base.
**Forest receipts**: timber, bamboo, minor forest produce and **red sanders** – endemic to the **Seshachalam hills**; seized red sanders logs are sold by **global e-auction/tender**.
**Sand**: under the **free sand policy (July 2024)** sand is supplied free (only loading and transport costs) – the State gave up sand as a revenue source (an earlier free-sand scheme ran in 2016).
Other heads: **interest** on loans to PSUs and local bodies, **dividends** from State PSUs, **education and medical fees**, **irrigation water rates**, port and power receipts.

Non-tax revenue is **small and volatile**: budget estimates regularly overshoot actuals – **2023-24 BE ₹15,400 crore** (mines ₹8,000 crore) against far lower collections; 2025-26 RE was cut by about a quarter.
**Bifurcation (2014)**: the **Hyderabad region** gave **nearly 50%** of undivided AP's tax and non-tax revenue; residual AP kept a land-, mineral- and agriculture-based receipts base.
With the **16th Finance Commission ending revenue-deficit grants**, AP must lean more on **own revenue**, including non-tax sources.

Ways to raise non-tax revenue: **auction of mineral blocks** (MMDR Amendment 2015 route), **critical and beach-sand minerals**, **rationalised user charges**, **asset and land monetisation**, better **PSU dividends**.
> Exam angle: non-tax = **₹11,474 cr (2026-27 BE)**; mining is the **largest** head (≈ ₹5,200 cr); royalty is **not a tax** (SC 2024); excise, stamps and vehicle tax are **tax** revenue.

mcqs.s: In the Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026-27, the State's own non-tax revenue was estimated at approximately how much?
mcqs.x: Own non-tax revenue 2026-27 BE is ₹11,474 crore; ₹64,362 crore is the share in central taxes and ₹1,25,846 crore is own tax revenue.

mcqs.s: Which of the following is the largest single source of Andhra Pradesh's own non-tax revenue in recent budgets?
mcqs.x: Mining receipts (₹5,196 crore in 2026-27 BE) are about 45% of AP's non-tax revenue.

mcqs.s: Which of the following is NOT a component of a State's own non-tax revenue in budget classification?
mcqs.x: State excise is a tax; royalty, dividends and forest receipts are non-tax revenue.

mcqs.s: In the Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026-27, non-tax revenue from mining was estimated at roughly how much?
mcqs.x: Mining non-tax revenue is ₹5,196 crore (2026-27 BE), slightly below ₹5,320 crore in 2025-26 RE.

mcqs.s: Andhra Pradesh's own non-tax revenue in the 2024-25 actual accounts stood at approximately how much?
mcqs.x: 2024-25 actual non-tax revenue was ₹5,972 crore; ₹89,435 crore was own tax revenue that year.

mcqs.s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold in July 2024 that royalty on minerals is not a tax?
o: India Cement v. State of Tamil Nadu
Mineral Area Development Authority v. SAIL
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
Goa Foundation v. Union of India
mcqs.x: The nine-judge bench (8:1) in MADA v. SAIL overruled India Cement (1989), which had called royalty a tax.

mcqs.s: By the 8:1 verdict of July 2024, which power was confirmed as belonging to the State legislatures?
o: Fixing coal royalty for all States
Taxing mineral rights and mineral-bearing land
mcqs.x: The Court held that States can tax mineral rights and mineral-bearing land; royalty is a contractual payment, not a tax.

mcqs.s: Which of the following statements about Andhra Pradesh's revenue receipts is correct?
o: State excise duty is the largest non-tax revenue head of the State.
Own non-tax revenue forms only about 5% of revenue receipts in 2026-27 BE.
Grants-in-aid from the Centre are part of the State's own non-tax revenue.
Share in central taxes is smaller than own non-tax revenue in 2026-27 BE.
mcqs.x: ₹11,474 crore of ₹2,34,140 crore is about 5%; grants are central transfers, excise is a tax, and the central tax share (₹64,362 crore) is far larger.

mcqs.s: Red sanders, a source of forest receipts for Andhra Pradesh, is endemic mainly to which hill range?
mcqs.x: Red sanders (Pterocarpus santalinus) is endemic to the Seshachalam and adjoining southern Eastern Ghats ranges.

mcqs.s: The present free sand policy of Andhra Pradesh, which gave up sand as a revenue source, was announced in:
mcqs.x: The free sand policy came in July 2024; sand is supplied free with only loading and transport costs (a similar scheme ran in 2016).

mcqs.s: Which of the following receipts of Andhra Pradesh is NOT counted under central transfers from the Union?
mcqs.x: Mining royalty is the State's own non-tax revenue; the other three come from the Centre.

mcqs.s: In 2025-26, Andhra Pradesh's non-tax revenue estimate of ₹19,119 crore was revised to about which figure?
mcqs.x: The 2025-26 RE is ₹14,324 crore, about 25% below the budget estimate – non-tax estimates are volatile.

mcqs.s: Which State public sector undertaking of Andhra Pradesh operates the Mangampet barytes mines that yield mining receipts?
mcqs.x: The AP Mineral Development Corporation (APMDC) mines barytes at Mangampet in Rayalaseema.

mcqs.s: Seigniorage fee collected by the AP Department of Mines and Geology is levied mainly on which minerals?
o: Minor minerals such as stone and gravel
mcqs.x: Seigniorage fee is the State's charge on minor minerals; royalty applies to major minerals.

mcqs.s: At bifurcation in 2014, the Hyderabad region had contributed nearly what share of undivided AP's tax and non-tax revenue?
mcqs.x: Hyderabad with Rangareddy and Medak gave nearly half of undivided AP's revenue.

mcqs.s: Which of the following is NOT a non-tax revenue source of the Andhra Pradesh Government?
mcqs.x: Taxes on vehicles are an own tax head; the others are non-tax receipts.

mcqs.s: The total revenue receipts of Andhra Pradesh in the Budget Estimates 2026-27 were placed at about:
mcqs.x: Revenue receipts are ₹2,34,140 crore; ₹3.32 lakh crore is the total budget size and ₹1,37,320 crore is own revenue.

mcqs.s: Andhra Pradesh's own revenue, that is own tax plus own non-tax revenue, in Budget Estimates 2026-27 is about:
mcqs.x: ₹1,25,846 crore own tax + ₹11,474 crore non-tax = ₹1,37,320 crore.

mcqs.s: Which of the following statements about State non-tax revenue is correct?
o: Stamps and registration fees are classified as non-tax revenue.
Royalty on major minerals is a non-tax receipt of the State.
Dividends from State PSUs are counted as tax revenue.
Non-tax revenue includes the State's share of central taxes.
mcqs.x: Royalty is non-tax revenue (and, per the SC in 2024, not a tax); stamps and registration is a tax head and the central tax share is a transfer.

mcqs.s: Which of the following is NOT a way for Andhra Pradesh to raise its non-tax revenue?
o: Raising the VAT rate on petrol
mcqs.x: A VAT increase raises tax revenue; the other measures raise non-tax receipts.

title: Bioremediation – Scope and Applications in India
bullets: **Why India needs it:** untreated sewage, industrial effluents, pesticides, plastics, oil spills and **legacy dumps**; bioremediation is **cheaper, decentralised and low-energy** with no secondary pollution, but adoption is still **mostly at pilot stage**.
**Rivers and drains:** CPCB lists **over 300 polluted river stretches**; **Namami Gange (NMCG)** has used **in-situ microbial bioremediation of drains** and **constructed wetlands**.

**NMCG Yamuna pilots:** constructed wetlands on the **Shastri Park and Kailash Nagar drains** (Delhi), about **10 MLD** combined, using **phytoremediation** plants and microbes; similar drain wetlands at **Rishikesh**.

**Legacy waste:** about **2,429 dumpsites**; **biomining** (microbial stabilisation + mechanical sorting) under **SBM-Urban 2.0 – 'Lakshya Zero Dumpsites'**; AP – Kapuluppada (Visakhapatnam), Ajit Singh Nagar (Vijayawada).

**Oil spills:** the **Indian Coast Guard** is the central coordinating authority under the **National Oil Spill Disaster Contingency Plan (NOS-DCP, 1996)**; microbes such as TERI–Indian Oil's **Oilzapper** use **hydrocarbon-degrading bacteria**.

**Major oil spills:** **MSC Chitra**, Mumbai (Aug 2010); BW Maple–Dawn Kanchipuram collision, **Ennore** (Jan 2017); Ennore creek oil after **Cyclone Michaung** (Dec 2023); **MSC Elsa 3** sinking off **Kerala** – oil and plastic nurdles (May 2025).

**Heavy metals:** **arsenic** in the **Ganga–Brahmaputra plains** (West Bengal, Bihar, Assam); **chromium** from **tanneries** (Kanpur) and chromium chemicals (**Ranipet**, TN) – microbes reduce toxic **Cr(VI) to less toxic Cr(III)**.
**Pesticide soils:** **endosulfan**-hit **Kasaragod (Kerala)** – aerial spraying on cashew; microbial degradation of organochlorines is studied for such sites.
**Textile and dye effluents:** **Tiruppur (Noyyal river)**; **white-rot fungi** decolourise dyes (they degrade lignin-like compounds).
**Crop residue:** **Pusa Decomposer** (**IARI**, 2020) – a fungal consortium that decomposes paddy stubble in the field, an alternative to **stubble burning**.
**Mine spoils:** reclaimed with grasses, legumes and **mycorrhizal fungi** (bio-reclamation).
**Indigenous microbes** adapted to India's heat, salinity and acidity often **outperform imported strains**.
**Institutions:** **DBT** (Clean Technology Programme), **BIRAC** (start-ups), **CSIR-NEERI Nagpur** (Phytorid), **TERI**, IITs, CPCB and SPCBs.

**Biosafety:** release of GE microbes is governed by the **Rules, 1989** under the **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986**; **GEAC (MoEFCC)** approves environmental release; **RCGM (DBT)** reviews research.
**BioE3 Policy (Aug 2024)** – **Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Employment**: biomanufacturing hubs; India's bioeconomy about **$165.7 billion (2024)**, target **$300 billion by 2030**.
**Linked missions:** **Swachh Bharat Mission**, **Namami Gange**, **National Clean Air Programme**; SDG 6 (clean water).
**Challenges:** slow and **site-specific**; complex pollutant mixtures; **heavy metals not completely removed**; no **national standards or protocols**; GMO biosafety; low awareness.
**Way forward:** national bioremediation and biomining protocols (**DBT + CPCB + SPCBs**), **regional hubs** linking universities, industry and local bodies, and **biosensor** monitoring.
> Exam angle: Coast Guard = oil-spill authority; Pusa Decomposer = IARI; GEAC approves GE microbes; Cr(VI) → Cr(III); arsenic belt = Ganga–Brahmaputra plains.

mcqs.s: Which agency is the central coordinating authority for responding to marine oil spills in Indian waters?
mcqs.x: Under the National Oil Spill Disaster Contingency Plan (1996), the Indian Coast Guard coordinates oil-spill response.

mcqs.s: The Pusa Decomposer, a microbial solution that decomposes paddy stubble in the field, was developed by which institute?
mcqs.x: IARI's Pusa Decomposer is a fungal consortium offered as an alternative to stubble burning.

mcqs.s: Oilzapper, a bacterial product for cleaning oily sludge and oil spills, was developed by TERI together with:
mcqs.x: TERI developed Oilzapper with Indian Oil Corporation; it uses hydrocarbon-degrading bacteria.

mcqs.s: Under which law are the 1989 Rules regulating the release of genetically engineered microbes in India framed?
o: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
mcqs.x: The Rules, 1989 for hazardous micro-organisms and GE organisms are made under the EPA, 1986.

mcqs.s: Which body under the Environment Ministry approves the environmental release of genetically engineered organisms, including microbes?
mcqs.x: The Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee (MoEFCC) approves release; RCGM under DBT reviews research.

mcqs.s: Chromium contamination needing remediation in India, as at Kanpur, is mainly linked to which industry?
mcqs.x: Tanneries use chromium salts; their effluents and sludge contaminate soil and water.

mcqs.s: In the bioremediation of chromium, microbes convert toxic hexavalent chromium into which less toxic form?
mcqs.x: Microbial reduction turns Cr(VI) (chromate, dichromate, CrO3) into far less toxic and less mobile Cr(III).

mcqs.s: Arsenic contamination of groundwater and soils in India is most serious in which region of the country?
mcqs.x: West Bengal, Bihar and Assam in the Ganga–Brahmaputra plains form India's arsenic belt.

mcqs.s: Kasaragod district of Kerala, a site of pesticide-contaminated soils, suffered from aerial spraying of which pesticide?
mcqs.x: Endosulfan was sprayed on cashew plantations; the Supreme Court banned it in 2011.

mcqs.s: White-rot fungi are used in bioremediation mainly for decolourising effluents from which industry?
mcqs.x: White-rot fungi break down lignin-like dye molecules, useful for textile effluents as in Tiruppur.

mcqs.s: Which of the following is NOT a national mission linked to bioremediation work in India?
mcqs.x: PM-KISAN is an income-support scheme; the others are linked to river, waste and pollution clean-up.

mcqs.s: Which of the following is NOT a limitation of bioremediation under Indian conditions?
o: It does not completely remove heavy metals
mcqs.x: Bioremediation is valued because it avoids secondary pollution; slowness, site-specificity and incomplete metal removal are real limits.

mcqs.s: Which of the following is NOT an application of bioremediation being taken up in India?
mcqs.x: Desalination uses reverse osmosis or distillation, not organisms.

mcqs.s: The BioE3 policy approved by the Union Cabinet in August 2024 stands for Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and:
mcqs.x: BioE3 = Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Employment; it promotes biomanufacturing.

mcqs.s: Which Union mission seeks 'Lakshya Zero Dumpsites' through biomining and bioremediation of legacy waste in cities?
mcqs.x: SBM-U 2.0 targets clearing all legacy dumpsites.

mcqs.s: Constructed wetlands used by NMCG for in-situ treatment of urban drains rely chiefly on which process?
mcqs.x: Wetland plants and root-zone microbes absorb, stabilise and degrade pollutants (e.g., Shastri Park drain pilot).

mcqs.s: Which of the following statements about bioremediation in India is correct?
o: Genetically engineered microbes can be released without any approval.
Bioremediation fully removes heavy metals like cadmium and lead.
Indigenous microbes adapted to local heat and salinity often outperform imported strains.
Bioremediation is costlier than incineration-based clean-up.
mcqs.x: Local strains suit Indian conditions; bioremediation is cheaper, does not fully remove metals, and GE release needs GEAC approval.

mcqs.s: The Department of Biotechnology supports bioremediation research and technologies mainly through which of its programmes?
mcqs.x: DBT's Clean Technology Programme funds bioremediation; BIRAC supports start-ups.

mcqs.s: Which ship's sinking off the Kerala coast in May 2025 caused a major oil and plastic nurdle spill?
mcqs.x: MSC Elsa 3 sank off Kerala in May 2025; MSC Chitra was Mumbai 2010 and Wakashio was Mauritius 2020.

mcqs.s: Microbial bioremediation of oil spills mainly uses which group of organisms to break down crude oil?
mcqs.x: Hydrocarbon-degrading bacteria (as in Oilzapper) metabolise oil into harmless products.

title: Soil Pollution – Sources, Effects and Control in India
bullets: **Soil pollution:** presence of **toxic substances** in soil above natural levels that harm **soil organisms, crops, animals and people**; FAO calls it a "**hidden reality**" (2018 symposium; Global Assessment of Soil Pollution, 2021).

**Sources:** **agro-chemicals** (fertilisers, pesticides), **industrial effluents and solid waste**, **mining and smelting**, urban waste and **sewage sludge**, **e-waste**, plastics, **acid rain**, oil spills, radioactive waste.

**Main pollutants:** **heavy metals** (lead, cadmium, mercury, arsenic, chromium), **persistent organic pollutants** (DDT, endosulfan, PCBs), PAHs, excess **nitrates and phosphates**, **microplastics** (plastic mulch).

**Diseases:** **Itai-itai** (Japan) – **cadmium**; **Minamata** (Japan, 1956) – **mercury**; blackfoot disease and arsenicosis (West Bengal) – **arsenic**; **fluorosis** – fluoride; **blue baby syndrome** – **nitrate**; nerve damage in children – **lead**.
**Biomagnification:** persistent pesticides like **DDT** build up in concentration along the food chain.
**Fertiliser imbalance:** recommended **N:P:K = 4:2:1**; heavy urea use in **Punjab–Haryana** distorts it; surplus **nitrate leaches** into groundwater.
**Pesticides:** India used about **67,000 tonnes** of chemical pesticides (2024-25); regulated by the **Insecticides Act, 1968** through the **Central Insecticides Board and Registration Committee**.
**Endosulfan:** aerial spraying on cashew in **Kasaragod (Kerala)**; **Supreme Court ban, 2011**; listed under the **Stockholm Convention** on POPs (2011).

**Industrial hot spots:** chromium – **Ranipet (TN)** and Kanpur tanneries; **Bhopal Union Carbide** site – **337 tonnes** of toxic waste moved to **Pithampur** for incineration (2025); informal **e-waste** recycling (Seelampur, Moradabad) leaks lead and cadmium.
**Reclamation of problem soils:** **acidic soils → lime**; **alkaline/sodic soils → gypsum**.
**Remediation methods:** bioremediation, **phytoremediation**, soil washing, immobilisation, organic amendments (compost, biochar).
**India has no separate soil-pollution law** – it is covered by the **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986** and the waste rules (Hazardous Waste Rules 2016, SWM Rules).

**Soil Health Card Scheme:** launched **19 Feb 2015 at Suratgarh (Rajasthan)**; **12 parameters** (N, P, K, S, Zn, Fe, Cu, Mn, B, pH, EC, organic carbon); **over 25 crore cards**; about **8,272 soil-testing labs**; since **2022-23** = '**Soil Health and Fertility**' under **RKVY**.
**Neem-coated urea** (100% from 2015) slows nitrogen release; **IFFCO Nano Urea** (2021) – the **world's first**.
**PM-PRANAM (2023):** States that cut chemical-fertiliser use get **50% of the subsidy saved** as a grant.
**National Mission on Natural Farming** (Cabinet, Nov 2024): **₹2,481 crore**, **1 crore farmers**, 7.5 lakh hectares.
**AP:** **APCNF** (Community-managed Natural Farming) run by **Rythu Sadhikara Samstha** since **2016** – won the **Gulbenkian Prize for Humanity 2024**.
**World Soil Day: 5 December** (FAO; first observed 2014); **International Year of Soils: 2015**.
> Exam angle: cadmium = itai-itai, mercury = Minamata; gypsum for alkaline, lime for acidic; Soil Health Card – Suratgarh 2015, 12 parameters; NPK 4:2:1; endosulfan ban 2011.

mcqs.s: Itai-itai disease, first reported in Japan, is caused by soil and water contamination with which heavy metal?
mcqs.x: Cadmium from mining waste in the Jinzu river basin caused itai-itai; mercury caused Minamata disease.

mcqs.s: Minamata disease, caused by industrial discharge in Japan in the 1950s, is linked to which heavy metal?
mcqs.x: Methylmercury from a chemical factory contaminated fish at Minamata Bay.

mcqs.s: Which material is commonly applied to reclaim alkaline or sodic soils affected by excess sodium salts?
mcqs.x: Gypsum (calcium sulphate) replaces sodium on soil particles; lime is used for acidic soils.

mcqs.s: Acidic soils, common in high-rainfall regions, are usually corrected by applying which soil amendment?
mcqs.x: Lime raises soil pH; sulphur and ammonium sulphate make soils more acidic.

mcqs.s: The Soil Health Card Scheme was launched in February 2015 at Suratgarh, which is located in which State?
mcqs.x: The scheme was launched on 19 February 2015 at Suratgarh, Sri Ganganagar district, Rajasthan.

mcqs.s: How many soil parameters are tested and reported on the Soil Health Card issued to farmers?
mcqs.x: Twelve: N, P, K, S, Zn, Fe, Cu, Mn, B, pH, EC and organic carbon.

mcqs.s: The commonly recommended ideal ratio of nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium fertiliser use for Indian soils is:
mcqs.x: NPK 4:2:1 is the standard recommendation; excess urea has skewed it in Punjab and Haryana.

mcqs.s: The Supreme Court of India banned the production and use of which pesticide in 2011?
mcqs.x: Endosulfan was banned after the Kasaragod tragedy; DDT is still allowed for vector control.

mcqs.s: Excess nitrate from fertilisers leaching into drinking water causes which condition in infants?
mcqs.x: Nitrate causes methaemoglobinaemia (blue baby syndrome), reducing the blood's oxygen-carrying capacity.

mcqs.s: Which law primarily regulates the registration, manufacture and sale of pesticides in India?
mcqs.x: The Insecticides Act, 1968 works through the Central Insecticides Board and Registration Committee.

mcqs.s: Under PM-PRANAM, States that reduce chemical fertiliser use receive what share of the subsidy saved as a grant?
mcqs.x: PM-PRANAM (2023) passes 50% of the fertiliser subsidy saved to the State as a grant.

mcqs.s: Andhra Pradesh Community-managed Natural Farming, winner of the Gulbenkian Prize for Humanity 2024, is implemented by:
mcqs.x: Rythu Sadhikara Samstha, a not-for-profit set up by the AP Government, runs APCNF since 2016.

mcqs.s: World Soil Day, promoted by the FAO to highlight the importance of healthy soils, is observed every year on:
mcqs.x: 5 December is World Soil Day; 5 June is Environment Day and 17 June is Desertification and Drought Day.

mcqs.s: Which of the following is NOT a significant source of soil pollution in India?
mcqs.x: Legume rotation improves soil fertility; the others add toxic substances to soil.

mcqs.s: Which of the following is NOT a heavy metal commonly associated with soil pollution?
mcqs.x: Calcium is a light, essential nutrient; cadmium, lead and mercury are toxic heavy metals.

mcqs.s: Which of the following is NOT a method of remediating soil polluted by heavy metals or pesticides?
mcqs.x: Biomagnification is the build-up of toxins along food chains, not a clean-up method.

mcqs.s: Which of the following statements about soil pollution in India is correct?
o: DDT breaks down quickly in soil and does not biomagnify.
Gypsum is the usual amendment to correct acidic soils.
India has no separate soil-pollution law; it is covered under the EPA, 1986.
Neem-coated urea speeds up the release of nitrogen in soil.
mcqs.x: Soil pollution falls under the EPA and waste rules; neem coating slows N release, gypsum is for alkaline soils, and DDT is persistent.

mcqs.s: Which of the following statements about the Soil Health Card Scheme is correct?
o: The card reports only nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium levels.
It now runs as 'Soil Health and Fertility' under the RKVY.
The scheme was launched in 2019 at Varanasi.
Cards are issued only to farmers owning above two hectares.
mcqs.x: Since 2022-23 it is a component of RKVY; it covers all farmers, reports 12 parameters and began in 2015 at Suratgarh.

mcqs.s: Toxic waste from the Union Carbide site in Bhopal was moved in 2025 for incineration to which place?
mcqs.x: About 337 tonnes of waste were taken to the Pithampur (Dhar district) facility for incineration.

mcqs.s: Which IFFCO product, launched in 2021 as the world's first of its kind, aims to cut excess urea use?
mcqs.x: IFFCO Nano Urea (liquid) was launched in 2021 to reduce granular urea use and nitrate pollution.

title: Applications of Radioisotopes – Medicine, Agriculture, Industry and Dating
bullets: **Radioisotope:** an unstable isotope that emits **alpha, beta or gamma** radiation; used as a **tracer** (detected in tiny amounts) or as a **radiation source**.

**India's supply chain:** isotopes made in **Trombay research reactors** (Dhruva, Apsara-U) and supplied by **BRIT – Board of Radiation and Isotope Technology** (DAE unit, **1989**, **Vashi, Navi Mumbai**); regulator **AERB (1983)**.
**Cobalt-60:** cancer **teletherapy** – **Bhabhatron** is BARC's indigenous telecobalt machine; also used to sterilise and irradiate.
**Iodine-131** – **thyroid** disorders and thyroid cancer; **Technetium-99m** – the **most widely used diagnostic imaging** isotope (half-life about **6 hours**, obtained from Mo-99).

**Sodium-24** – blood circulation and **blood clots**; **Iron-59** – iron metabolism and **anaemia**; **Phosphorus-32** – blood disorders; **Iridium-192** – **brachytherapy**; **Lutetium-177** – targeted therapy of **neuroendocrine and prostate cancers**.
**Radiation sterilisation:** **ISOMED, Trombay (1974)** – India's first plant for **gamma sterilisation of medical products** (syringes, sutures, gloves).
**Radiation Medicine Centre (BARC), Parel, Mumbai** – India's nuclear-medicine centre.
**Agriculture – tracers:** **Phosphorus-32** tracks **fertiliser uptake** by plants.

**Mutation breeding:** gamma rays create useful mutants – BARC has released **72 'Trombay' crop varieties** (groundnut the most, 17); **Kaveri Vaaman** – India's **first mutant banana** (Nov 2025, with ICAR-NRCB Tiruchirappalli).
**Sterile Insect Technique:** males sterilised by **gamma radiation** are released to suppress pests.
**Food irradiation:** **low dose (< 1 kGy)** stops **sprouting of onion and potato** and delays ripening; **medium dose (1–10 kGy)** kills insects and pathogens; food does **not become radioactive**.

**Food irradiation in India:** **28 plants (2025), 22 private**; **KRUSHAK, Lasalgaon (Nashik)** onion unit (2002); **Radura** logo; irradiated **mangoes exported to the USA**; rules – **Atomic Energy (Radiation Processing of Food and Allied Products) Rules, 2012**.

**Industry:** **gamma radiography** of welds and castings (**Ir-192, Co-60**) – non-destructive testing; **radiotracers** find leaks in **pipelines and dams**; gamma scanning of refinery columns; thickness and level **gauges**.
**Consumer uses:** **Americium-241** in **smoke detectors**; **tritium** in self-luminous signs and watch dials.

**Dating:** **Carbon-14** (half-life **5,730 years**) – **radiocarbon dating** of once-living matter up to about 50,000 years – **Willard Libby** (Nobel Chemistry 1960); **uranium–lead** and **potassium–argon** methods date rocks and the Earth.
**Hydrology:** **tritium** and environmental isotopes trace groundwater recharge and age.
**Space:** **Plutonium-238** powers **radioisotope thermoelectric generators (RTGs)** on deep-space probes (Voyager, Curiosity).
**Units:** activity – **becquerel** (old: curie); absorbed dose – **gray**; equivalent dose – **sievert**.
**Accidents:** **Mayapuri, Delhi (2010)** – **Cobalt-60** from a discarded gamma cell in scrap; **Goiânia, Brazil (1987)** – Caesium-137.
> Exam angle: Co-60 = cancer teletherapy; I-131 = thyroid; Tc-99m = imaging; C-14 = dating (Libby, 5,730 years); Na-24 = clots/leaks; P-32 = fertiliser uptake; Am-241 = smoke detector; BRIT = Vashi.

mcqs.s: Which radioisotope is used in teletherapy machines like Bhabhatron for treating cancer patients?
mcqs.x: Bhabhatron, BARC's indigenous teletherapy machine, uses a Cobalt-60 gamma source.

mcqs.s: Which radioisotope is widely used for the diagnosis and treatment of thyroid disorders?
mcqs.x: The thyroid concentrates iodine, so I-131 is used to image and treat it.

mcqs.s: The radioisotope most widely used in diagnostic nuclear medicine imaging, with a half-life of about six hours, is:
mcqs.x: Tc-99m, obtained from Molybdenum-99, is the workhorse of diagnostic scans.

mcqs.s: Radiocarbon dating, used to find the age of fossils and archaeological remains, was developed by which scientist?
mcqs.x: Willard Libby developed C-14 dating and won the 1960 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

mcqs.s: The half-life of carbon-14, which forms the basis of radiocarbon dating, is approximately:
mcqs.x: C-14's half-life is about 5,730 years; 12.3 years is tritium and 4.5 billion years is U-238.

mcqs.s: Which radioisotope is used as a tracer to study the uptake of phosphatic fertilisers by plants?
mcqs.x: P-32 labelled fertiliser shows how much phosphorus a crop absorbs.

mcqs.s: Which radioisotope is commonly used to detect blood clots and leaks in underground pipelines?
mcqs.x: Short-lived Na-24 is a tracer for blood circulation and for locating pipeline leaks.

mcqs.s: Which radioisotope is found in common ionisation-type smoke detectors used in homes and offices?
mcqs.x: Am-241 ionises air in the detector chamber; smoke disrupts the current and sets off the alarm.

mcqs.s: Which unit of the Department of Atomic Energy at Vashi, Navi Mumbai, supplies radioisotopes and radiation technology products?
mcqs.x: The Board of Radiation and Isotope Technology (1989) supplies isotopes and radiation equipment.

mcqs.s: The radiation dose used to stop sprouting of onions and potatoes in storage falls in which range?
mcqs.x: Sprout inhibition needs only a low dose (below 1 kGy); medium doses are used to kill insects and pathogens.

mcqs.s: BARC's first radiation-induced mutant banana variety, released in November 2025, is known by which name?
mcqs.x: Kaveri Vaaman (TBM-9) came from gamma-irradiated Grand Naine, developed with ICAR-NRCB, Tiruchirappalli.

mcqs.s: BARC has released about how many improved crop varieties through radiation-induced mutation and cross-breeding as of 2025?
mcqs.x: BARC's tally of Trombay varieties reached 72 with the Kaveri Vaaman banana in 2025.

mcqs.s: India's first gamma radiation plant for sterilising medical products, ISOMED, was set up in 1974 at:
mcqs.x: ISOMED at Trombay, Mumbai, sterilises syringes, sutures and other medical products with gamma rays.

mcqs.s: In space missions, the radioisotope Plutonium-238 is used mainly for which purpose?
mcqs.x: Heat from Pu-238 decay is turned into electricity in RTGs on probes like Voyager and Curiosity.

mcqs.s: Which of the following is NOT an application of radioisotopes in medicine, agriculture or industry?
o: Fixing atmospheric nitrogen in the soil
mcqs.x: Nitrogen fixation is done by bacteria such as Rhizobium; the others use radioisotopes.

mcqs.s: Which of the following methods is NOT used to determine the age of rocks or fossils?
mcqs.x: Tc-99m is a short-lived medical imaging isotope; the other three are dating methods.

mcqs.s: Which of the following is NOT a unit related to radioactivity or radiation dose?
mcqs.x: The decibel measures sound intensity; becquerel (activity), gray (absorbed dose) and sievert (equivalent dose) relate to radiation.

mcqs.s: Which of the following statements about food irradiation in India is correct?
o: Food irradiation in India uses only alpha rays.
Irradiated food does not become radioactive at the permitted doses.
Irradiation of onions is banned in India.
All food irradiation plants in India are government-owned.
mcqs.x: Gamma rays, X-rays or electron beams do not make food radioactive; onions are irradiated at Lasalgaon, and 22 of 28 plants are private.

mcqs.s: The Mayapuri radiation accident of 2010 in Delhi involved scrap metal containing which radioisotope?
mcqs.x: A discarded gamma cell with Cobalt-60 sources was sold as scrap at Mayapuri; Cs-137 was involved at Goiânia (1987).

mcqs.s: The Sterile Insect Technique controls insect pests by releasing males that have been sterilised using:
mcqs.x: Gamma-irradiated sterile males mate with wild females, which then lay no viable eggs.

title: Solid Waste – Meaning, Sources and Classification
bullets: **Solid waste:** discarded material in solid or semi-solid form – domestic, commercial, institutional, market and street waste, drain silt, horticulture and dairy waste – managed under the **SWM Rules** (industrial hazardous, biomedical and e-waste have **separate rules**).

**By source:** **residential**, **commercial**, **institutional** (schools, offices), **municipal services** (street sweeping, parks, drains), **construction and demolition**, **industrial**, **agricultural**, **biomedical**, **mining**.
**By nature:** **biodegradable / organic** (food, garden waste, paper) vs **non-biodegradable / inorganic** (plastic, glass, metal).
**By hazard:** **hazardous** (ignitable, corrosive, reactive, toxic) vs **non-hazardous**.
**By combustibility:** **combustible** (paper, plastics, textiles, wood → **refuse-derived fuel, RDF**) vs **non-combustible** (glass, metals, stones, ash).
**By recyclability:** recyclable **dry waste** (paper, plastic, metal, glass) vs **residual inert waste** (sand, debris).

**SWM Rules 2026 – four streams:** **wet** (green bin – kitchen and garden waste), **dry** (blue – paper, plastic, metal, glass), **sanitary** (red – **diapers, sanitary napkins**), **special care** (black – **batteries, bulbs, medicines, paint cans**).

**Terms:** **refuse** = all solid waste; **garbage** = putrescible food and market waste; **rubbish** = non-putrescible (paper, tins, glass); **ashes** = residue of burning; **leachate** = polluted liquid seeping from landfills; **inert waste** = non-reactive (sand, debris).

**Bio-Medical Waste Rules 2016 colours:** **yellow** – anatomical waste, soiled dressings (incineration); **red** – contaminated recyclable plastics (tubing, catheters, gloves); **white translucent** – **sharps** (puncture-proof); **blue** – glassware and metallic implants.

**Separate rules by waste type:** Plastic Waste Management Rules 2016; **E-Waste (Management) Rules 2022** (in force **1 April 2023**); **Bio-Medical Waste Rules 2016**; **Hazardous and Other Wastes Rules 2016**; **Battery Waste Management Rules 2022**; **C&D Waste Rules 2016**.
**Indian municipal waste:** about **1.5 lakh tonnes a day** (CPCB 2021-22) with collection near **98%**; **biodegradable organic matter is the largest share (~55–60%)**.
**Industrial solid waste:** **fly ash** (coal thermal plants – largest), **red mud** (alumina), **phosphogypsum** (fertiliser), **slag** (steel).
**Agricultural waste:** crop residue (stubble), **paddy husk, cattle dung** – biodegradable; dung → biogas under GOBARdhan.
**Mining waste:** **overburden** and **tailings**.
**E-waste:** India is the **world's third-largest generator** (after China and the USA – Global E-waste Monitor 2024).
**Management hierarchy:** **reduce → reuse → recycle → recover (energy) → dispose (landfill, least preferred)**.
**AP:** **CLAP (2021)** gave 3-bin sets (green, blue, red) to households; all **123 ULBs** under Swarna Andhra–Swachh Andhra.
> Exam angle: four streams (2026) – wet, dry, sanitary, special care; BMW colours – yellow, red, white (sharps), blue (glass); leachate; garbage vs rubbish; fly ash = largest industrial waste.

mcqs.s: Under the Solid Waste Management Rules 2026, waste must be segregated at source into how many streams?
mcqs.x: Wet, dry, sanitary and special care – four streams (the 2016 Rules had three).

mcqs.s: Under the SWM Rules 2026, used batteries, bulbs, expired medicines and paint cans belong to which waste stream?
mcqs.x: Domestic hazardous items form the special care stream (black bin).

mcqs.s: Under the Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules 2016, sharps such as needles are placed in which colour container?
mcqs.x: Sharps go into puncture-proof white translucent containers; blue is for glassware.

mcqs.s: In biomedical waste segregation, human anatomical waste and soiled dressings are placed in which colour bag?
mcqs.x: Yellow-category waste is sent for incineration or deep burial.

mcqs.s: Contaminated recyclable plastic waste such as tubing, catheters and gloves from hospitals goes into which colour bag?
mcqs.x: Red-category waste is autoclaved or disinfected and then recycled.

mcqs.s: The contaminated liquid that seeps out of a landfill after rainwater percolates through waste is called:
mcqs.x: Leachate can pollute groundwater; sullage is kitchen and bathroom wastewater.

mcqs.s: Which term refers to the putrescible, rapidly decomposing kitchen and market waste generated in a city?
mcqs.x: Garbage is putrescible; rubbish is non-putrescible waste like paper and tins.

mcqs.s: Which industrial solid waste is generated in the largest quantity by coal-based thermal power plants?
mcqs.x: Fly ash is the largest industrial solid waste; red mud comes from alumina refining.

mcqs.s: The E-Waste (Management) Rules 2022, which replaced the 2016 Rules, came into force from which date?
mcqs.x: The E-Waste (Management) Rules 2022 took effect on 1 April 2023 with an EPR certificate system.

mcqs.s: According to the Global E-waste Monitor 2024, India ranks where among the world's largest e-waste generators?
mcqs.x: India is third after China and the USA.

mcqs.s: Concrete, bricks and rubble from building works are classified under which category of solid waste?
mcqs.x: C&D waste is mostly inert and has its own rules.

mcqs.s: Which of the following is NOT a basis used for classifying solid waste?
mcqs.x: Waste is classed by source, nature, hazard, combustibility and recyclability – not by colour.

mcqs.s: Which of the following is NOT classified as dry waste for source segregation?
mcqs.x: Vegetable peels are wet (biodegradable) waste for the green bin.

mcqs.s: Which of the following is NOT a separate set of waste management rules notified by the Centre?
mcqs.x: There are rules for battery, e-waste and biomedical waste; there is no separate textile waste rule.

mcqs.s: Which of the following statements about the classification of solid waste is correct?
o: Garbage refers to non-putrescible waste like tins.
Paper is a non-biodegradable part of municipal waste.
Fly ash is classified as biomedical waste.
Glass and metals are non-combustible parts of municipal waste.
mcqs.x: Glass and metals do not burn; paper is biodegradable, fly ash is industrial waste and garbage is putrescible.

mcqs.s: Which of the following statements about municipal solid waste in India is correct?
o: Construction debris is classified as hazardous waste.
Biodegradable organic matter forms the largest share of it.
Cities collect less than 20% of the waste generated.
Plastics form more than half of it.
mcqs.x: Organic matter is about 55–60%; collection is near 98% and C&D debris is mostly inert.

mcqs.s: The combustible fraction of municipal waste, processed into fuel for cement kilns, is known as:
mcqs.x: RDF is made from dry combustibles such as plastics, paper and textiles.

mcqs.s: Under the SWM Rules 2026, used diapers and sanitary napkins must be placed in which waste stream?
mcqs.x: The 2026 Rules created a separate sanitary stream (red bin); under 2016 they went wrapped into dry waste.

mcqs.s: Crop residues, cattle dung and paddy husk are examples of which category of solid waste?
mcqs.x: Farm residues are biodegradable agricultural waste.

mcqs.s: Overburden and tailings are solid wastes produced mainly by which economic activity?
mcqs.x: Overburden is rock removed to reach ore; tailings are residues left after ore processing.

title: Industrial Development in India – Patterns, Regions and Problems
bullets: **Policy phases:** IPR **1948** → IPR **1956** (**Mahalanobis model**, heavy industry, public sector) → licence raj → **NIP 1991** (delicensing, LPG) → **Make in India (2014)** → **PLI schemes (2020-21)** → **National Manufacturing Mission** (Budget 2025-26).
**Eight major industrial regions (NCERT):** Mumbai–Pune, Hugli, Bengaluru–Chennai, Gujarat, Chotanagpur, **Visakhapatnam–Guntur**, Gurugram–Delhi–Meerut, Kollam–Thiruvananthapuram.
**Location theory:** **Alfred Weber's least-cost theory (1909)** – transport, labour and agglomeration costs.

**Raw-material-oriented** industries: iron and steel (Chotanagpur), **cement near limestone**, sugar near cane; **market-oriented**: consumer goods; **port-based**: refineries – **Jamnagar**, the **world's largest single-site refinery**; **footloose**: software, electronics.
**ASI 2023-24:** GVA leaders – **Maharashtra (~16%)**, Gujarat (~14%), Tamil Nadu (~10%); **Tamil Nadu first in number of factories and in employment**.
**Growth:** IIP grew **4.0% (2024-25)** and **4.1% (2025-26, provisional)**; IIP is released monthly by the **NSO (MoSPI)**.

**Industrial corridors:** **NICDP – 11 corridors**; first = **Delhi–Mumbai Industrial Corridor** (node **Dholera**); **Aug 2024** – **12 industrial smart cities** (₹28,602 crore) including **Orvakal and Kopparthy (AP)**.
**PLI schemes:** **14 sectors**, **₹1.97 lakh crore** (2021).
**MSME definition (from 1 April 2025):** micro – investment up to **₹2.5 crore**, turnover ₹10 crore; small – ₹25 crore / ₹100 crore; medium – ₹125 crore / ₹500 crore.
**Regional imbalance remedies:** backward-area incentives – APRA **Section 94** (AP), **UNNATI 2024** for the **North-East**.
**Industrial sickness:** **SICA 1985** created **BIFR (1987)**; repealed in 2016 – now handled under the **Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016** through the **NCLT**.
**Delayed payments to MSMEs:** buyers must pay within **45 days** under a written agreement (MSMED Act); enforced through **Income Tax Section 43B(h)** from **2023-24**.
**Informality and scale:** most manufacturing jobs are in **unorganised units**; the '**missing middle**' of medium firms limits productivity and exports.
**Pollution:** CPCB's **Comprehensive Environmental Pollution Index (CEPI)** identifies **critically polluted industrial clusters** (e.g., **Vapi, Ankleshwar**).

**Other problems** (see host notes): infrastructure and **logistics cost**, capacity under-use, land and labour rigidities, credit gap, **low R&D**, **import dependence** on China, **jobless growth**.
**AP pattern:** coastal belt – **Visakhapatnam–Guntur** region; **Visakhapatnam–Chennai Industrial Corridor** (first leg of the East Coast Economic Corridor); **Sri City** SEZ.
> Exam angle: 8 NCERT regions; Weber 1909; ASI – Maharashtra (GVA), TN (factories, jobs); IIP by NSO; SICA/BIFR → IBC; MSME micro ₹2.5 crore; 45-day payment rule.

mcqs.s: Which of the following is one of the eight major industrial regions of India identified in NCERT geography?
mcqs.x: Visakhapatnam–Guntur is one of the eight major industrial regions along with Hugli, Chotanagpur and others.

mcqs.s: The least-cost theory of industrial location, which stresses transport costs, was put forward in 1909 by:
mcqs.x: Alfred Weber's theory; Christaller gave central place theory and von Thünen agricultural location.

mcqs.s: According to the Annual Survey of Industries 2023-24, which State ranked first in the number of factories?
mcqs.x: Tamil Nadu leads in factories and industrial employment; Maharashtra leads in GVA.

mcqs.s: According to ASI 2023-24, which State had the largest share of industrial Gross Value Added in India?
mcqs.x: Maharashtra had about 16% of industrial GVA, ahead of Gujarat and Tamil Nadu.

mcqs.s: As per provisional data, India's Index of Industrial Production grew by about how much in 2025-26?
mcqs.x: IIP growth was about 4.1% in 2025-26 against 4.0% in 2024-25.

mcqs.s: The Index of Industrial Production for India is compiled and released every month by which body?
mcqs.x: The NSO under MoSPI releases the IIP; DPIIT's Office of the Economic Adviser releases the core industries index.

mcqs.s: In August 2024, the Union Cabinet approved 12 industrial smart cities, including Orvakal and Kopparthy, under which programme?
mcqs.x: The 12 new nodes (₹28,602 crore) are under NICDP; Orvakal and Kopparthy are in Andhra Pradesh.

mcqs.s: Under the MSME definition revised from April 2025, a micro enterprise can have investment of up to:
mcqs.x: Micro limits are now ₹2.5 crore investment and ₹10 crore turnover (earlier ₹1 crore and ₹5 crore).

mcqs.s: The Production Linked Incentive schemes announced in 2021 with an outlay of ₹1.97 lakh crore covered how many sectors?
mcqs.x: PLI covers 14 sectors including mobiles, pharma, autos, textiles and solar modules.

mcqs.s: The Sick Industrial Companies Act 1985 and the BIFR have been replaced by which legal framework?
mcqs.x: SICA was repealed in 2016; sick firms are now resolved under the IBC through the NCLT.

mcqs.s: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956, which gave priority to heavy industries, was based on which growth model?
mcqs.x: The Second Plan and IPR 1956 followed P.C. Mahalanobis's heavy-industry strategy.

mcqs.s: Which place in Gujarat has the world's largest single-site oil refinery, an example of port-based industry?
mcqs.x: Reliance's Jamnagar complex is the world's largest single-site refinery.

mcqs.s: The Comprehensive Environmental Pollution Index, used to identify critically polluted industrial clusters, is prepared by:
mcqs.x: CPCB's CEPI flags clusters such as Vapi and Ankleshwar.

mcqs.s: Under Section 43B(h) of the Income Tax Act, buyers with a written agreement must pay MSME suppliers within how many days?
mcqs.x: The MSMED Act caps payment at 45 days; Section 43B(h) denies the deduction if payment is late.

mcqs.s: Which of the following is NOT a major problem of industrial development in India?
o: Abundant cheap credit for small firms
mcqs.x: MSMEs face a credit gap and high cost of capital; the others are recognised problems.

mcqs.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the eight major industrial regions of India listed in NCERT?
mcqs.x: Indore–Dewas–Ujjain is a minor industrial region; Hugli, Chotanagpur and Mumbai–Pune are major ones.

mcqs.s: Which of the following is NOT a raw-material-oriented industry usually located near its raw material?
mcqs.x: Software is footloose; cement, sugar and steel are located near limestone, cane and ore/coal.

mcqs.s: Which of the following statements on industrial development in India is correct?
o: The 2011 target of a 25% manufacturing share was achieved by 2022.
BIFR continues to handle sick companies today.
The 1991 policy increased industries reserved for the public sector.
Tamil Nadu leads in industrial employment as per ASI 2023-24.
mcqs.x: Tamil Nadu tops employment; the 25% target was missed, BIFR was abolished and 1991 cut reserved industries from 17 to 8.

mcqs.s: UNNATI, the industrialisation scheme approved by the Union Cabinet in 2024, aims to promote industry in which region?
mcqs.x: UNNATI (Uttar Poorva Transformative Industrialization Scheme) is for the North-East.

mcqs.s: Which was the first industrial corridor taken up under India's corridor programme, with Dholera as a key node?
mcqs.x: DMIC (2007) was the first; Dholera in Gujarat is its flagship smart city.

title: Industrial Incentives – APRA Section 94 and AP's Policies 4.0 (2024-29)
bullets: **Why incentives:** to offset the **loss of Hyderabad's industrial base** at bifurcation, attract investment and balance regions (Rayalaseema, North Coastal AP).

**APRA 2014, Section 94(1):** the Centre shall take **fiscal measures, including tax incentives**, to promote industrialisation and economic growth in both successor States; **94(2)** – backward-area infrastructure.

**Finance Act 2015** gave tax incentives to **notified backward areas of AP, Telangana, Bihar and West Bengal**: **Section 32AD – investment allowance of 15%** of the cost of new plant and machinery installed **1 April 2015 – 31 March 2020**; asset not to be sold for **5 years**.
**Additional depreciation of 35%** (instead of the normal **20%**) on such new machinery (Section 32(1)(iia)).
**Backward districts:** **7** – four of Rayalaseema and three of North Coastal AP; a special development grant of about **₹50 crore per district per year**.
**Special Category Status** (with tax holidays) was **not granted**; the Centre offered a **Special Assistance Measure** instead.

**AP Industrial Development Policy (IDP) 4.0, 2024-29:** target **₹30 lakh crore** investment; investment bands – **sub-large ₹50–500 crore, large ₹501–1,000 crore, mega ₹1,001–5,000 crore, ultra-mega above ₹5,000 crore**.

**IDP 4.0 incentives:** **capital subsidy** (up to **30% of fixed capital investment** for early-bird projects), employment-linked top-up (up to 10%), **decarbonisation subsidy up to 6% of FCI**, **net SGST reimbursement**, **power-cost reimbursement**, **stamp-duty and land-conversion reimbursement**, top-up for **central PLI** projects; overall cap as a share of FCI.

**MSME and Entrepreneur Development Policy 4.0:** '**One Family One Entrepreneur**' (an entrepreneur in every family by 2030); **10% higher capital subsidy** for **SC, ST, BC, women and differently-abled** entrepreneurs; **₹500 crore** corpus; **175 MSME parks** (one per Assembly constituency).

**Electronics Manufacturing Policy 4.0:** **100% net SGST** reimbursement for **5 years**; power subsidy **₹1 per unit** for 5 years; **100% stamp duty** reimbursement; recruitment help **₹4,000 (men) / ₹6,000 (women)** a month for six months.

**Integrated Clean Energy Policy 4.0:** target **₹10 lakh crore** and 7.5 lakh jobs; RE land lease **₹31,000 per acre per year**; **NALA charges exempted**; RE manufacturing – **25% capital subsidy**, 100% SGST, power ₹1/unit for 10 years.
**Food Processing Policy 4.0:** ₹30,000 crore investment, 3 lakh jobs; plus a **Private Industrial Parks** policy (plug-and-play parks, worker housing).
Together the 2024-29 policies aim at about **20 lakh jobs**.
**Speed of Doing Business:** **Single Desk Portal** (time-bound clearances); **State Investment Promotion Board (SIPB)**, chaired by the **CM**, approves large projects and incentive packages.

**Central incentives used in AP:** **PLI**, **SEZ Act 2005** (Sri City), **Section 115BAB – 15% corporate tax** for new manufacturing companies (production by 31 March 2024), NICDP nodes (**Orvakal, Kopparthy**).
**Issues:** pending **incentive arrears** strain the budget; incentive competition among States; benefits favour large firms.
> Exam angle: **32AD = 15%** investment allowance; **additional depreciation 35%**; Sec **94(1)** = tax incentives; IDP 4.0 bands; 'One Family One Entrepreneur'; 175 MSME parks.

mcqs.s: Under the Finance Act 2015, new plant and machinery in notified backward areas of AP earned an investment allowance of:
mcqs.x: Section 32AD gives a 15% investment allowance; 35% is the enhanced additional depreciation.

mcqs.s: Units in notified backward areas of Andhra Pradesh got additional depreciation at what rate, instead of the normal 20%?
mcqs.x: Additional depreciation was raised from 20% to 35% for new machinery in these areas.

mcqs.s: Which section of the Income Tax Act provides the investment allowance for notified backward areas of AP and Telangana?
mcqs.x: Section 32AD was inserted in 2015; 10AA is for SEZ units and 115BAB for new manufacturing companies.

mcqs.s: Which section of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 mandates fiscal measures, including tax incentives, for industrialisation?
mcqs.x: Section 94(1) covers tax incentives; Section 90 is about Polavaram and Section 5 about the capital.

mcqs.s: Under AP Industrial Development Policy 4.0 (2024-29), an ultra-mega project requires an investment above about:
mcqs.x: Ultra-mega projects exceed ₹5,000 crore; mega projects are ₹1,001–5,000 crore.

mcqs.s: AP's MSME and Entrepreneur Development Policy 4.0 promotes which slogan for entrepreneurship in every household?
mcqs.x: The policy aims at an entrepreneur in every family by 2030.

mcqs.s: Under AP's Electronics Manufacturing Policy 4.0, eligible units get what share of net SGST reimbursed for five years?
mcqs.x: Net SGST is fully reimbursed for five years, along with ₹1/unit power subsidy and stamp duty reimbursement.

mcqs.s: Under AP's MSME Policy 4.0, enterprises of SC, ST, BC, women or differently-abled entrepreneurs get how much extra capital subsidy?
mcqs.x: They get a 10% higher capital subsidy.

mcqs.s: AP Industrial Development Policy 4.0 offers a separate subsidy of up to 6% of fixed capital investment for:
mcqs.x: A decarbonisation subsidy of up to 6% of FCI rewards green investments.

mcqs.s: Andhra Pradesh plans how many MSME parks, roughly one per Assembly constituency, under its 2024-29 policies?
mcqs.x: AP has 175 Assembly constituencies; 294 was undivided AP's number and 26 is the district count.

mcqs.s: Under AP's Integrated Clean Energy Policy 4.0, land for renewable energy projects is leased at about how much per acre per year?
mcqs.x: The lease rate is ₹31,000 per acre per year, with NALA charges exempted.

mcqs.s: Which body, chaired by the Chief Minister, approves large investment proposals and their incentives in Andhra Pradesh?
mcqs.x: The SIPB, headed by the CM, clears large projects and incentive packages.

mcqs.s: Section 115BAB of the Income Tax Act offered which concessional corporate tax rate to new manufacturing companies?
mcqs.x: New manufacturing companies starting production by 31 March 2024 could opt for 15%; 22% is the general concessional rate (115BAA).

mcqs.s: Under AP Industrial Development Policy 4.0, a mega project falls within which investment band?
mcqs.x: Bands: sub-large ₹50–500 crore, large ₹501–1,000 crore, mega ₹1,001–5,000 crore, ultra-mega above ₹5,000 crore.

mcqs.s: Which of the following is NOT an incentive offered under AP Industrial Development Policy 4.0?
mcqs.x: A State policy cannot exempt central taxes; the others are State incentives.

mcqs.s: Which of the following is NOT among the 2024-29 '4.0' policies announced by Andhra Pradesh?
mcqs.x: The 4.0 set includes Industrial, MSME, Food Processing, Electronics, Clean Energy and Private Parks policies.

mcqs.s: Which of the following States was NOT covered by the 2015 tax incentives for notified backward areas?
mcqs.x: Section 32AD covered AP, Telangana, Bihar and West Bengal.

mcqs.s: Which of the following statements on industrial incentives for Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: Section 94 incentives apply only to Telangana.
The 2015 investment allowance covered assets installed from April 2015 to March 2020.
Special Category Status with tax holidays was granted to AP in 2015.
IDP 4.0 is meant only for micro and small enterprises.
mcqs.x: 32AD covered 2015-2020; SCS was denied, Section 94 covers both States, and IDP 4.0 is for large projects (MSMEs have their own policy).

mcqs.s: Under AP's Electronics Manufacturing Policy 4.0, what power subsidy do eligible units receive for five years?
mcqs.x: A power subsidy of ₹1 per unit for five years.

mcqs.s: Which multi-product SEZ in Tirupati district is Andhra Pradesh's leading example of incentive-driven industrial growth?
mcqs.x: Sri City hosts auto, electronics and food processing units; Orvakal and Kopparthy are new NICDP nodes.
